reference: Martin & Moyce (1952) dam-break front trajectory — independent digitisation used as a cross-check

source.paper: Martin, J.C. & Moyce, W.J. (1952). An experimental study of the collapse of liquid columns on a rigid horizontal plane. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences, 244(882), 312-324.
source.digitisation_origin: Value-identical with the digitisation distributed inside Lethe's official dam-break post-processing (LETE-CFD/lethe, dam-break Martin & Moyce example).
source.transcription_path: Transcribed from the frozen anchor table of the sibling solver repositories in this workspace: m9 benchmarks/pending/dam_break_sc/result.json, key `reference_digitisation_lethe` (14 points), which records the value-identity claim to Lethe's script. Not re-digitised here and not verified against the paywalled original.
source.caveat: Neither this table nor the bundled one has been checked against the archived paper text: the 1952 paper is paywalled and figure-level digitisation is the only access route. The two tables are independent transcriptions, so their spread is a lower bound on the reference uncertainty.

convention.dependent_variable: X = x_front / a, so Z/a = X - 1 for the front measured from the initial column edge (Martin & Moyce measure from the wall).
convention.aspect_ratio: column height / width = 2, matching the bundled table and the case configuration in src/tensorsph/dam_break.py.
